_comment: RICS precision, native emtk windows. Drawn by emtk.view_form over PrecisionViewModel (gui/view_model.py): 'settings' is the left window, 'numbers' the table window. The plot, the file dialog, Help and Guide are drawn by gui/app.py. Field names, ranges, decimals and descriptions are those of precision.view.json (the Qt AutoForm spec).
title: RICS precision

sections.title: Settings
sections.name: settings
sections.description: What you are measuring and how you plan to scan it.
Predict the precision for the settings below, or export the numbers behind the curve.

buttons.label: Predict
buttons.description: Sweep the pixel dwell time and predict the relative error on D, marking your own setting on the curve. The sweep runs in the background.

buttons.label: Export CSV
buttons.description: Write the predicted error against dwell time (dwell, line, frame, error) to a CSV file.

sections.title: Sample

sections.label: D [µm²/s]
sections.description: The diffusion coefficient you expect to measure. This is the awkward part of planning a scan: the best settings depend on the answer you do not have yet, so use a literature value or a guess and check how sensitive the prediction is to it. A free dye is a few hundred; a labelled protein a few tens; a membrane protein below one.

sections.label: Molecules in view
sections.description: Number of fluorescent molecules in the illuminated region. Too few and the correlation is noisy; too many and its amplitude (which goes as 1/N) sinks into the background.

sections.label: Brightness [kHz/molecule]
sections.description: Photons per second from a single molecule at the centre of the focus. This is the dominant lever on precision after the number of frames — a dim label cannot be rescued by scanning cleverly.
The sample settings of the planned measurement. Click the header to fold or unfold.

sections.title: Optics

sections.label: w_r [µm]
sections.description: Lateral beam waist. Measure it with the waist calibration rather than guessing: every predicted error scales with it.

sections.label: w_z [µm]
sections.description: Axial beam waist. Only its ratio to w_r matters here.

sections.label: Pixel size [nm]
sections.description: Physical pixel size. It should sample the waist several times over — around 4 to 6 pixels across w_r — or the spatial shape of the correlation is undersampled.

sections.label: Membrane (2-D)
sections.description: Use the 2-D geometry for a membrane or a surface, which has different shape factors from a 3-D focus.
The optics settings of the planned measurement. Click the header to fold or unfold.

sections.title: Scan

sections.label: Pixel dwell [µs]
sections.description: The dwell time you plan to use. It is marked on the curve so you can see how far it sits from the optimum.

sections.label: Line overhead ×
sections.description: How much longer a line takes than the sum of its pixels, from flyback and settling. 1.2 means 20 % overhead. The sweep scales the line time with the dwell, because a line cannot stay short as its pixels grow.

sections.label: Pixels per line
sections.description: Image width. A larger image averages more pixel pairs and so measures better, at the cost of a longer frame.

sections.label: Lines per frame
sections.description: Image height.

sections.label: Frames
sections.description: Frames averaged. Precision improves as the square root of this, so halving the error costs four times the acquisition time.
The scan settings of the planned measurement. Click the header to fold or unfold.

sections.title: Estimator

sections.label: Lags fitted
sections.description: Largest lag included on each axis. Cost grows as the fourth power of this, so raising it is expensive; the reference implementation uses 15. It must stay below half the smaller image dimension — a lag is averaged over the pixel pairs that realise it, and a small image holds too few.

sections.label: Repeats
sections.description: Monte-Carlo realisations behind each point. The predicted error carries an uncertainty of roughly 1/sqrt(2N) itself — about 11 % at 40 — which is why the position of the minimum is only good to an order of magnitude.

sections.label: Seed
sections.description: Random seed, so a quoted prediction can be reproduced.
The estimator settings of the planned measurement. Click the header to fold or unfold.

sections.title: Numbers
sections.name: numbers
sections.description: The numbers behind the curve.
One row per swept dwell time: the line and frame time it implies and the predicted error (a click on a header sorts by that column). N/A in the error column means the timing is not realisable.

columns.title: Line [ms]
columns.tooltip: Line time implied by the dwell and the overhead.

columns.title: Frame [ms]
columns.tooltip: Time for one frame — multiply by the frame count for the total acquisition.

columns.title: Error [%]
columns.tooltip: Predicted relative error on D. N/A means the timing is not realisable.
